question.text: As per SEBI norms governing mutual fund distribution, what must non-individual intermediaries (such as MFD entities) ensure with respect to EUIN on client transaction forms and feeds?

answer.text: They must use the same EUIN of the principal officer on every transaction regardless of who actually interacted with the investor
The employee or relationship representative who actually advised the investor must quote his or her valid EUIN on the application form or in the transaction feed, alongside the entity's ARN
Quoting an EUIN is optional and need only be done at the discretion of the AMC
EUINs are required only for direct-plan transactions and not for regular-plan transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: The Employee Unique Identification Number (EUIN) framework is designed to identify the specific individual employee or representative of a non-individual distributor who has actually interacted with or advised the investor. SEBI requires that on each client application form (and in the related transaction feed) the EUIN of that employee/representative is quoted along with the distributor entity's ARN, so that the chain of advice can be traced back to a specific person. This also supports eligibility to receive Regular Plan commissions on the transaction at the entity level. The Trap: Using a single EUIN (such as the principal officer's) regardless of who actually advised the investor defeats the very purpose of EUIN-level traceability. Treating EUIN disclosure as optional contradicts the standing SEBI requirement. Restricting EUINs to direct-plan transactions is incorrect — direct plans by definition do not involve an intermediary's advice, whereas EUIN is associated with the advised, distributor-routed flow on regular plans. Note: The cited workbook chapter supports the requirement that intermediaries ensure EUINs are quoted on application forms or transaction feeds for employees/representatives who interact with investors. The specific consequence referenced in the earlier formulation of this question — a signed investor declaration that no advice was received when EUIN is missing — is not in the cited workbook pages. The framing above reflects the workbook-supported EUIN disclosure requirement and general industry practice rather than the missing-EUIN declaration consequence.
